detail.title: Thermodynamic and Practical Costs of Memory Reliability
detail.summary: Memory reliability and retention time are fundamentally limited by energy dissipation. Our revision incorporates findings that non-equilibrium environments and non-reciprocal couplings modulate Landauer erasure costs, establishing that predictive power in information engines is constrained by available energy and coarse-grained state access.
detail.reason: Revision required to integrate new dissipation bounds and non-equilibrium evidence into the memory reliability model.

detail.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory Reliability (Revised)
detail.summary: Energy costs and retention times in physical memories are fundamentally bounded by coarse-graining and non-equilibrium dissipation constraints.
detail.reason: Revising the notebook to integrate new evidence on coarse-grained entropy production and channel memory.
